publication_endpoint: independent test of capture-time migratory readiness x landscape resistance on later movement expression
core_hypothesis: movement capacity is gated by internal readiness, and the ecological cost of landscape resistance depends on that readiness

primary_cohort.rationale: each stage has >=98 individuals across 7 projects with complete WRS-table coverage

boundary_groups.FII: n=17; 16/17 from one project, descriptive boundary only
boundary_groups.silver: coarse stage label; not pooled into ordinal Durif analysis

primary_predictions: capture-time Durif stage predicts later migration initiation/progression
WRS/barrier effects differ among FIII/FIV/FV stages
stage x landscape interaction is stable to leaving one project out

primary_estimands.stage_effect: effect of capture-time Durif stage on later movement expression

falsification: stage effect disappears after project/design covariate control
landscape resistance does not interact robustly with stage
interaction is driven by one project
effect requires post-hoc regrouping of Durif stages
evidence_boundary: aggregate successful-migrant counts by stage were inspected during development; Europe-wide panel is independent developmental evidence, not outcome-blind confirmation
eog_role: discovery of an extreme resident anchor only
